scenario_description:
Objective: Get the newly delivered tub transfer bench assembled and stable before tonight's planned bathing routine.
Emerging Need: The assembly begins, then stops when a missing leg-lock button leaves one leg sliding instead of locking level.
Decision Context: A saved occupational-therapy home-safety note and current communications determine whether replacement parts, improvising, or same-day maintenance assistance remains viable.
Consequence: If the maintenance window passes, the bench cannot support tonight's routine and the bath-safety setup remains blocked rather than merely pending.

parameter.subject: Tub transfer bench delivered today
parameter.body: Your replacement tub transfer bench was delivered to the apartment mail room this morning. The package includes the frame, four adjustable legs, and the small-parts bag needed for assembly.

parameter.title: Assemble tub transfer bench
parameter.description: Set up the delivered bench before the evening bathing routine; check that all legs lock level before use.

parameter.content: Starting the transfer-bench assembly now. The frame is on the bathroom mat and I’m sorting the leg-height pins before I put it in the tub.
Assembly has stopped: the left rear leg is missing its spring lock button, so it slides instead of clicking at any height. The included small-parts bag is already empty.

parameter.subject: Auto-reply: missing spring lock button report
parameter.body: We received your missing-part report for the tub transfer bench. Current spring lock button replacements for this model cannot ship before Monday, April 13; retail exchanges depend on unreserved store stock.

parameter.content: The onsite maintenance desk stopped taking same-day resident repair assists at 5:30 PM. Non-emergency bathroom hardware requests received now roll to tomorrow afternoon.
